description:
src/mailbox.rs handle_mailbox_set at line 477-480 calls get_objects::<Mailbox>(caller, &account_id, None, None) to fetch ALL mailboxes for role-uniqueness and name+parentId duplicate checks. A second full fetch at line 914 happens before the destroy phase. 

For IMAP-scale accounts (commonly 100s to low 1000s of mailboxes; corporate accounts can exceed 10k), every Mailbox/set request — including ones that just create a single new mailbox — pays an O(n) full-mailbox-fetch cost. Two such fetches per request when destroys are present.

The matching JMAP-g7wu.6 work pushed Mailbox/query filter+sort INTO the backend precisely to avoid this kind of full-fetch. Mailbox/set role-uniqueness and name-uniqueness validation belong in the backend for the same reason (and could be enforced via DB unique constraints atomically with the mutation).

The handler comment at lines 466-476 documents the RFC 8620 §5.3 pre-mutation-snapshot reason for the fetch. That reasoning is correct for the same-request swap logic, but the role-uniqueness check itself could be a single targeted query rather than a full fetch.

Low-priority because the alternative would require a substantial backend trait reshape (a 'check role uniqueness within tx' method or similar). Noted for the production-backend handoff.
title: Mailbox/set fetches full mailbox list per request — O(n) on IMAP-scale accounts
